\caption{Median latency in milliseconds for the same aggregate written
three ways in SQL, on 232,828 admitted rows over
28 facets, against the fused single pass. A bold
percentage is the share of queries that \emph{completed}: at
$\eps=10^{-3}$ PostgreSQL aborts the naive form on overflow, and
aborts the textbook max-shifted form on \emph{underflow}, because its
\texttt{float8} \texttt{exp} raises in both directions; only the
explicitly guarded rewrite completes, at ten times the naive form's
cost. DuckDB saturates to infinity instead, so the naive form returns
NaN for some facets and the max-shift does repair it. The DuckDB rows
and the fused pass aggregate the same precomputed similarities, which
isolates the aggregation plan; PostgreSQL computes the similarity
itself through the vector extension with sequential scan forced.}
